n: Now Zephaniah turns back to Jerusalem itself: woe to the rebellious, defiled, oppressive city. After judging the nations, he reveals God’s own city is guilty too.
Four failures: she didn’t listen, didn’t accept correction, didn’t trust the Lord, and didn’t draw near to God.
Her officials are like roaring lions and her judges like wolves that devour everything by morning.

f.w: they gnaw not the bones till the morrow
f.g: They leave nothing — not even bones — until morning.

n: Her prophets are reckless and unfaithful; her priests profane what is holy and twist the law.

f.w: her priests have polluted the sanctuary

n: Yet the righteous Lord is right there in the city. He never does wrong; morning by morning He reveals His justice — but the unjust feel no shame.

f.w: every morning doth he bring his judgment to light

n: God has destroyed other nations and left their cities empty as a warning.
God hoped Jerusalem would learn and fear Him so it wouldn’t be destroyed. Instead they eagerly did even more evil.

f.g: They were eager — they hurried to do wrong.

n: So “wait for me,” says the Lord, until the day He rises to gather the nations and pour out His anger. The whole earth will be consumed by His jealous fire.
Then a beautiful turn: God will give the peoples pure lips, so all can call on His name and serve Him together — a reversal of the confusion of languages at Babel.

f.g: Literally “a pure lip” — speech purified for worship.
Literally “with one shoulder” — side by side, united.

f.w: turn to the people a pure language

n: From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia, God’s scattered worshipers will bring Him offerings. The gathering reaches the ends of the earth.

f.w: From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia

n: On that day Jerusalem won’t be shamed by past sins, because God will remove the proud. No one will be arrogant on His holy mountain again.

f.w: thou shalt no more be haughty

n: God will leave a humble, lowly people who take refuge in the Lord’s name.
This faithful remnant will do no wrong and tell no lies. Like sheep, they will graze and rest with nothing to fear.

f.w: neither shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth

n: Sing, shout, rejoice with all your heart, daughter of Zion! The mood shifts from judgment to celebration.
The Lord has removed your punishment and driven out your enemy. The King of Israel — the Lord Himself — is with you. Never again fear disaster.

f.w: the king of Israel, even the LORD

n: On that day Jerusalem will hear: “Don’t be afraid; don’t let your hands hang limp.”

f.w: Let not thine hands be slack

n: A tender verse: the mighty Lord is in your midst to save you. He will delight in you with joy, quiet you with His love, and rejoice over you with singing. God sings over His people!

f.w: he will rejoice over thee with joy
he will rest in his love
f.g: Or “He will quiet you by His love” — or be silent in His love.

n: God will gather those who grieved because they couldn’t attend the sacred festivals, those who bore the shame of exile.

f.g: The appointed sacred feasts at the temple.

n: God will deal with all oppressors, save the lame, gather the outcasts, and turn their shame into praise everywhere.

The book ends with promise: God will bring His people home, gather them, and make them honored among all peoples, restoring their fortunes before their eyes. Latter-day Saints see this in the gathering of Israel.

f.w: At that time will I bring you again
